financials_interim.company_name: HNB Life PLC (formerly HNB Assurance PLC)
financials_interim.notes: COMPANY basis (HNB Life PLC standalone, life insurance shareholders' fund). Composite (life + general) insurer, not a bank/NBFI -- no COGS/gross-profit concept and no loan book, so a different adaptation than the project's bank convention is used. revenue = 'Net Income' (Net Earned Premium + Total Other Revenue), the filing's own all-in top-line subtotal before benefits/claims/expenses -- the closest analogue to 'total revenue' for an insurer under SLFRS 4. operating_profit left blank -- the filing discloses Profit Before Taxation directly with no separate operating-profit subtotal (Finance and Other Insurance Related Costs is disclosed and captured under finance_costs instead). cost_of_sales/gross_profit/current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory left blank -- the Statement of Financial Position is presented in order of liquidity with no current/non-current classification and no inventory concept. trade_receivables is mapped to 'Premium Receivables' and trade_payables to 'Reinsurance Payable' as the closest operating analogues (amounts due from/to policyholders and reinsurers respectively) -- these are NOT conventional trade debtors/creditors and this substitution should be treated as approximate. short_term_borrowings = 'Bank Overdrafts' (the only genuinely interest-bearing short-term facility disclosed); long_term_borrowings left blank -- no debentures or term loans disclosed. Lease Creditors excluded from borrowings (operating lease liabilities under SLFRS 16, not conventional debt). Insurance Contract Liabilities (Life and General) are the dominant liability but are policyholder obligations, not borrowings, and are left out of the short/long-term borrowings fields entirely, consistent with never treating policyholder/customer liabilities as debt. Company adopted the CA Sri Lanka Statement of Alternative Treatment and continued to apply SLFRS 4 (not SLFRS 17) for this Q2 interim, so figures are not yet on the new insurance-contracts basis; comparative 1H2025 figures are also on the SLFRS 4 / LKAS 39 basis and have not been restated. Balance-sheet identity (assets = liabilities + equity) and EPS cross-check (PAT / 150,000,000 shares) both tie out exactly for Company and Group -- no column-swap issues found in this filing.

interim_updates.company_name: HNB Life PLC (formerly HNB Assurance PLC)
interim_updates.note_text: HNB Life PLC's Group gross written premium grew 29% YoY to LKR 18,370Mn for 1H2026 (1H2025: LKR 14,269Mn), with Life Insurance GWP up 43% to LKR 12,343Mn and General Insurance (subsidiary HNB General Insurance Ltd) GWP up 7% to LKR 6,027Mn. Group net earned premium rose 37% to LKR 14,851Mn and total revenue (Net Income) rose 29% to LKR 19,668Mn, but Group PBT grew only 13% to LKR 826Mn (1H2025: LKR 730Mn) as premium growth was diluted by a 57% jump in Net Insurance Benefits and Claims (to LKR 6,058Mn) and an 11% rise in the Change in Contract Liabilities - Life Fund (to LKR 6,436Mn). By segment, the Life Insurance shareholders' fund PBT was essentially flat at LKR 618,576k (1H2025: LKR 606,973k, +1.9%), while the General Insurance subsidiary's PBT surged 68% to LKR 207,733k (1H2025: LKR 123,441k) -- General Insurance alone accounted for roughly 88% of the Group's LKR 95.9Mn PBT increase. Group net profit margin (PAT/total revenue) compressed to 3.0% from 3.4% a year earlier despite the profit growth, since revenue grew faster than profit. Total Comprehensive Income for the Group fell 15% to LKR 448Mn (1H2025: LKR 530Mn) even though PAT grew 14%, because Other Comprehensive Income swung to a LKR 144Mn loss (1H2025: LKR 10Mn gain) on a large net unrealised fair-value loss on Available-For-Sale bonds of LKR 814Mn (1H2025: LKR 463Mn gain) -- a swing of over LKR 1.27Bn attributable to rising market yields during the period, roughly half of which is absorbed by the Life Policyholders' AFS Reserve Fund rather than shareholders' equity.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for HASU -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. YoY uses the filing's own six-month comparative column (1H2025); a like-for-like three-month (Q2-only) comparison was also available in the filing but the six-month cumulative view was used as primary, consistent with how LKAS 34 interim reporting and the company's own statements present it.
interim_updates.takeaway: Premium growth (+29% GWP) and profit growth (+14% PAT) look strong, but almost all of the Group's PBT improvement came from the General Insurance subsidiary (+68% PBT) while the core Life Insurance business was essentially flat (+1.9% PBT); at the same time, a LKR 814Mn unrealised bond fair-value loss dragged Group Total Comprehensive Income down 15% and total equity fell to LKR 13,216Mn from LKR 14,133Mn at FY2025 year-end, so the reported profit growth did not translate into growth in book value this period.
operational_highlights: Group PBT +13% YoY to LKR 826Mn; Group PAT +14% YoY to LKR 593Mn (1H2026 vs 1H2025)
Gross written premium +29% Group to LKR 18,370Mn: Life Insurance GWP +43% to LKR 12,343Mn, General Insurance GWP +7% to LKR 6,027Mn
General Insurance subsidiary PBT +68% to LKR 207.7Mn (1H2025: LKR 123.4Mn); Life Insurance shareholders' fund PBT roughly flat at LKR 618.6Mn (+1.9%)
Net Insurance Benefits and Claims +57% to LKR 6,058Mn and Change in Contract Liabilities - Life Fund +11% to LKR 6,436Mn, both diluting premium growth at the PBT line
Group Total Comprehensive Income -15% to LKR 448Mn despite profit growth, on a LKR 814Mn net unrealised fair-value loss on AFS bonds (1H2025: LKR 463Mn gain)
Basic/diluted EPS (Group) +14% to LKR 3.95 (1H2025: LKR 3.46); interim dividend of LKR 750Mn paid during the period (1H2025: LKR 585Mn)
key_drivers: General Insurance subsidiary (HNB General Insurance Ltd) PBT +68% to LKR 207.7Mn -- the primary driver of Group PBT growth, contributing roughly 88% of the LKR 95.9Mn Group PBT increase

Rising Net Insurance Benefits and Claims (+57% to LKR 6,058Mn) and Change in Contract Liabilities - Life Fund (+11% to LKR 6,436Mn) offset most of the premium growth at the Life Insurance segment level

LKR 814Mn net unrealised fair-value loss on Available-For-Sale bonds (vs LKR 463Mn gain a year earlier), a roughly LKR 1.27Bn negative swing, driven Group Total Comprehensive Income down despite higher reported PAT

Company has elected the CA Sri Lanka Statement of Alternative Treatment to continue reporting under SLFRS 4 (not SLFRS 17) for this Q2 interim; SLFRS 17/9 transition impact remains qualitative-only pending the FY2026 annual financial statements
